title: RFID for Hospitality — Key Cards & Linen Tags
summary: Hospitality RFID replaces magnetic-stripe and metal keys across hotel rooms, resort amenities and cruise cabins using ISO/IEC 14443 Type A contactless cards and IP67 wristbands compatible with the dormakaba Saflok, ASSA ABLOY VingCard / Visionline, Salto XS4, Onity Advance and Be-Tech lock fleets. Proud Tek manufactures MIFARE DESFire EV3 ({chip:nxp-mifare-desfire-ev3:crypto.algorithm}, NXP MF3DH series) cards for new-build and chain-scale properties, MIFARE Plus SE for Classic-to-AES migrations, and MIFARE Classic 1K for legacy Saflok RT and Onity HT estates, alongside NTAG 424 DNA cashless wristbands integrated with Tappit and Connect&GO POS platforms. Field data shows magnetic-stripe re-issue rates dropping 85-95% within 90 days, cashless F&B per-capita spend up 15-30%, and end-of-stay cash reconciliation falling from 90 minutes to 8 minutes per property. ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 cards, PCI DSS 4.0 and GDPR compliant.
heroPoints: Lock-system compatible across Saflok, Onity, ASSA ABLOY Visionline, Salto, VingCard and Be-Tech — send us your lock model, we verify the chip before we quote.

Three credential tiers: {chip:nxp-mifare-desfire-ev3:crypto.algorithm} DESFire EV3 for new-build and security-sensitive properties, Plus SE for Classic-to-AES migrations, Classic 1K for legacy Saflok RT / Onity HT estates.
Chain-scale stock program: 72-hour dispatch on reorders, buffer inventory per property, property-specific artwork across 50–500+ keyed-alike portfolios.

sections.title: What Proud Tek supplies to the hospitality industry
sections.intro: Three small pieces of RFID quietly run a hotel: the card that opens the door, the band on the guest's wrist at the pool, and the tag sewn into the towel. Proud Tek is a factory-direct manufacturer of exactly those three product lines — guest key cards, guest wristbands (pool, spa, all-inclusive) and linen / laundry tags. We do not sell locks, PMS software or reader infrastructure; we supply the credential and the tag, verified against the lock, reader or laundry system the property already operates.

sections.title: Guest wristbands for pool, spa and all-inclusive
sections.intro: Once guests leave the room, RFID moves from the card in their pocket to the band on their wrist. Here the decision has less to do with the chip and more to do with band material, water exposure and how long the guest keeps it on — a day-pass at a water park and a two-week all-inclusive are not the same problem.

sections.title: Linen and laundry tracking — where the ROI is easiest
sections.intro: Linen tracking is the hospitality RFID project with the shortest payback period, and the reason is refreshingly unglamorous: towels, robes and sheets walk out the door. A 200-room property loses them to guest souvenir-taking, mis-sorted laundry returns and the quiet, unaccounted attrition nobody budgets for — and a tag that survives the wash puts a number on all three.

sections.intro: Ask any hotel-lock integrator what to specify on a new build and you'll get the same answer with almost no hesitation. It's worth understanding why the industry converged so firmly on one chip generation — and why the one still sitting in millions of older locks is quietly on the clock.

sections.title: Compatibility, compliance and what to ask the lock vendor
sections.intro: The two technical conversations every hospitality RFID buyer should have before cutting a PO — one with the lock vendor, one with the card supplier.
bullets: Confirm ISO/IEC 14443 Type A — every MIFARE family credential we supply conforms to ISO/IEC 14443-2/-3/-4, which is the only RF baseline hotel locks actually need to accept.
Confirm the chip generation is supported by the installed lock firmware: Classic 1K, Plus SE or DESFire EV3. Ask the lock vendor for the exact chip-family allow-list their firmware recognises.
For DESFire EV3 deployments, agree the key ceremony — who holds the AES master key, who diversifies per-property, who provides the HSM — before you ship the first production card.

For laundry, confirm whether the property wants HF (13.56 MHz, short-range tunnel) or UHF (860–960 MHz, overhead portal) linen tags. The tag family and reader stack are tied together; mixing is a procurement trap.
For ISO/IEC 7810 branded print, confirm the artwork is produced for ID-1 CR80 dimensions and that any chip-side personalisation runs against the same PMS card-number scheme.
checklist: Inventory every lock model across the portfolio before specifying any card chip.
Run a 500-card pilot per property before committing to a 50,000+ stock order.
Write the key ceremony + chip-transition plan before the migration PO, not during it.
Stage artwork under one master account with per-property overlays — avoids drift across 50+ hotels.
Agree a 72-hour reorder SLA and a buffer level tied to monthly run rate, not ad-hoc emails.

faq.question: Which chip should I pick for my hotel locks?
faq.answer: Chip choice follows lock model and firmware. Legacy Saflok RT/MT and Onity HT run on {chip:nxp-mifare-classic-1k:short_name}; newer Saflok Quantum / Confidant RFID and Onity Advance typically support MIFARE Plus or DESFire EV3; ASSA ABLOY Visionline and Salto XS4 are natively DESFire-generation. Send us the lock model plate, firmware version and a working card — we confirm the chip via a lab-side read before we quote.

faq.question: What is the MOQ and lead time for custom-printed hotel key cards?
faq.answer: Custom-printed MOQ is 500 cards, with 10–15 business days production plus freight. Blank white stock cards ship from 100 pieces, typically within 1–3 business days. Volume pricing improves materially at 10,000+ cards per PO; chain accounts run on a blanket PO with 72-hour reorder dispatch.

faq.question: Can you supply one account for a multi-property hotel chain?
faq.answer: Yes. We currently supply chains ranging from 10 to 500+ properties under a single master account. Per-property artwork, per-property card numbering schemes and consolidated monthly billing are standard. Volume pricing improves on cumulative monthly run rate across the portfolio rather than per-property POs.

faq.question: How do RFID wristbands tie into cashless F&B at an all-inclusive?
faq.answer: The wristband carries a {chip:nxp-mifare-desfire-ev3:short_name} or NTAG424 DNA chip bound to the guest folio in the PMS. Pool, spa and F&B POS terminals tap the wristband and post the charge to the room. Cashless uplift typically runs 15–30 % versus cash-handling properties because the friction of opening a wallet disappears; staffing at amenity gates also drops because the tap-to-verify flow replaces visual wristband checks.

faq.question: Will my linen survive 200+ wash cycles with a tag sewn in?
faq.answer: PPS laundry tags are specified at 300-500 industrial wash cycles at 90 °C and typically outlast the garment itself. Textile/woven tags run 200-300 cycles with the most garment-like feel. Silicone tags are 50-100 cycles and are better for direct-skin wear (robes, uniforms). The failure mode is almost never the chip — it is the sewing or heat-seal attachment, which we specify alongside the tag.

faq.question: How do I handle the migration from {chip:nxp-mifare-classic-1k:short_name} to DESFire EV3 without a lockout?
faq.answer: Stage the lock firmware upgrade first so the fleet accepts both Classic and DESFire credentials during the transition. Then issue DESFire cards to new guests while existing Classic cards remain active through their stay. Sunset Classic issuance over a 30–60 day window. We hold both chip SKUs in stock during the transition so no property is left without cards. The key ceremony (who holds the AES master key and who diversifies per property) needs to be agreed before the first DESFire card ships.

faq.question: Are branded wooden or bamboo key cards reader-compatible?
faq.answer: Yes — our wooden and bamboo card bodies use the same MIFARE Classic / Plus / DESFire chips as the PVC equivalents and present identical RF to the lock reader. Read range is within specification (per ISO/IEC 14443) once we verify the antenna tuning under the chosen veneer. We always pilot 100 cards per lock model before ramping a wooden-card order.

faq.question: What chip is used in MIFARE hotel keys?
faq.answer: Three NXP silicon families dominate hotel keys in 2024-2026. {chip:nxp-mifare-classic-1k:short_name} (CRYPTO-1, 1 KB EEPROM) remains the installed base for legacy dormakaba Saflok RT / MT and Onity HT locks but is academically broken since the Garcia et al. ESORICS 2008 paper. MIFARE Plus SE is the AES-128 drop-in replacement that preserves the same reader infrastructure during migration. {chip:nxp-mifare-desfire-ev3:short_name} (NXP MF3DH series, AES-128 plus 3DES, 2/4/8 KB user memory, up to 28 application slots) is the new-build default specified by ASSA ABLOY Visionline, Salto XS4 and dormakaba Confidant RFID. See the NXP product brief at https://www.nxp.com/products/rfid-nfc/mifare-hf/mifare-desfire/.

faq.question: Is {chip:nxp-mifare-classic-1k:short_name} secure enough for hotel keys?
faq.answer: No — not for new deployments. The CRYPTO-1 cipher has been cryptanalysed since 2008 (Garcia et al., ESORICS); commercially available tools clone Classic 1K cards in under 30 seconds. For an installed Saflok RT or Onity HT fleet that has not yet migrated, Classic 1K remains operationally serviceable for short-stay rooms with low theft exposure, but should be retired in favour of MIFARE Plus SE (AES-128, same reader infrastructure) or {chip:nxp-mifare-desfire-ev3:short_name} (AES-128, AES mutual auth, multi-application). The NIST recommendation NIST SP 800-131A treats CRYPTO-1 as deprecated; PCI DSS 4.0 also penalises stored-value cards on broken ciphers. Plan a Classic-to-DESFire migration within 12-24 months.

faq.question: Can you supply ASSA ABLOY VingCard or Saflok-compatible key cards directly?
faq.answer: Yes. Proud Tek manufactures the underlying contactless credential ({chip:nxp-mifare-classic-1k:short_name}, Plus SE, DESFire EV3) used in ASSA ABLOY Global Solutions VingCard / Visionline / Mobile Access locks and in dormakaba Saflok Quantum / Confidant RFID locks. We do not resell branded lock-vendor stock; we supply the chip on ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 (CR80, 85.60 x 53.98 x 0.76 mm) PVC, wood, bamboo or metal card bodies with your artwork. Compatibility is verified property-by-property against the lock firmware version. References: ASSA ABLOY Global Solutions hospitality documentation at https://www.assaabloyglobalsolutions.com/en/hospitality and dormakaba Saflok product pages at https://www.dormakaba.com.
